listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Friday, October 30. Our lead story is a major crypto hack. Binance has been hit by a hack worth six point three billion dollars. It is suspected to be the largest in history. Two analytics firms have attributed the incident to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor. The BBC has also published an explainer on what is known so far. The size and the attribution are still described as suspected, so expect more detail to follow. Now the front page. The Atlanta Braves exercised Ronald Acuña Junior's seventeen million dollar option. They also exercised a seven million dollar option on second baseman Ozzie Albies. In architecture tech, Snaptrude has launched an AI agent for BIM workflows. It covers concept design, BIM modelling, MEP and construction documentation. For Claude builders, the Claude Platform added a beta Usage and Cost Analytics API. It reports token usage and cost for Console and Enterprise organizations. In national news, grand jury subpoenas were sent to election workers in Los Angeles. They come amid rising tension between the Trump administration and California officials over the state's voter rolls. Now the sections. In tech and AI, Simon Willison notes OpenAI's new API credits benefit for eligible ChatGPT subscriptions. In politics, The Lever reports that Texas candidate Gina Hinojosa is campaigning against the established Democratic approach. Drop Site News reports on the arrest of Bolivia's attorney general. In world news, the United States and Japan agreed to set up a Japanese facility for joint missile production. China also elevated a military general to the Politburo. In sports, a set of trade deadline grades looks at the DeForest Buckner deal. The 49ers are sticking with kicker Eddy Pineiro despite his struggles. And in the UFC, Quillan Salkilld will face Benoît Saint Denis in Sydney in February. In Atlanta, a veteran homebuilder sees Blue Ridge as the next frontier for metro Atlanta housing. Star Community Bar will close on December thirty first after thirty five years in Little Five Points. In architecture, AEC Magazine asks how many meters Autodesk wants to attach to its computing stack. ArchDaily also marks one hundred years since the birth of Brazilian architect Assis Reis. In science and nature, GPS tracking shows seabirds get jet lag on fast east-west flights. NASA-funded scientists also dated a Mars meteorite to more than four point one billion years old. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Crypto giant Binance hit by $6.3bn hack suspected to be largest in history
lead.note: Crypto giant Binance has been hit by a hack worth $6.3 billion, which is suspected to be the largest in history. Two analytics firms have attributed the incident to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor. The BBC has also published an explainer on what is known so far, written by business reporter Archana Shukla. The attribution comes from analytics firms, and the size of the hack is described as suspected, not confirmed. For this reader, who follows technology closely, the story shows how large the sums moving through crypto platforms have become, and how quickly a single incident can reach into the billions. The summaries do not say how the breach happened, so further reporting is likely to fill in the details.
